headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline can write shared files and use MCP/network, while RisingWave is a non-runnable data system with no documented isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; its session scope is per-VS Code workspace with shared state via filesystem. RisingWave has no documented interactive surface, so direct injection into it is not evidenced. The plausible risk is Cline ingesting attacker-controlled workspace content or MCP output as instructions.
conditions: IF Cline is pointed at a workspace containing untrusted files or MCP outputs
IF any downstream automation parses those files as instructions
mitigations: Restrict Cline to a clean workspace
Disable or whitelist MCP servers
Separate instruction files from data files
Require manual review before tool actions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for workspace content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline can read the filesystem, run browsers, and has broad network egress, so sensitive workspace data could leave the local environment. RisingWave is documented as non-runnable with no IO surfaces, so it is not the leakage source; the pairwise risk is Cline exfiltrating shared workspace data if such data is present.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the VS Code workspace
IF Cline is allowed to send those contents to its configured model provider or browser
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace
Use a redacted test workspace
Disable network egress for the session
Rotate any exposed credentials
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can modify git state and write the filesystem; RisingWave is not runnable and exposes no write capabilities in the profile. There is no documented overlapping mutable surface, so a direct capability conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is limited because the pair lacks a shared writable target in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same git repository or directory
IF RisingWave is wrapped in an external process that writes into Cline's workspace
mitigations: Keep RisingWave outside the workspace tree
Use separate repositories or mounts
Lock git operations during Cline runs
Review any generated patches before apply
requires-engineering: add workspace-level write locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived content, and file edits that a downstream system may treat as authoritative. RisingWave has no documented verification or action-taking behavior here, so the cascade is inferred rather than directly evidenced. The main risk is Cline's output being reused without validation in a data pipeline or code change.
conditions: IF Cline's generated artifacts are consumed by an automated pipeline
IF RisingWave or surrounding tooling applies those artifacts without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of generated artifacts
Add schema and unit-test checks
Compare outputs against source data
Limit Cline to draft-only changes
requires-engineering: add verification gates before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Cline is documented as handling model provider API keys and browser screenshots, while RisingWave has no documented data classes or residency/compliance claims. The only concrete compliance concern is Cline touching secrets or screenshots in a workspace; there is no evidence of a specific residency mismatch with RisingWave, so this remains a limited gap.
conditions: IF the workspace contains regulated data or secrets
IF Cline's configured model provider stores prompts or screenshots outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Disable screenshot capture when unnecessary
Confirm provider retention settings
Use a local or approved model endpoint
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
